title: Pasta for a Hangover: Does It Help? (Plus Mac and Cheese)
excerpt: Is pasta good for a hangover? What carbs actually do the morning after, whether mac and cheese helps or hurts a queasy stomach, and the best ways to eat pasta when you feel rough.
metaDescription: Is pasta good for a hangover? What carbs really do the morning after, whether mac and cheese helps or hurts, and the gentlest ways to eat pasta.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** pasta is a solid, gentle hangover food, but not a cure. A bowl of plain or lightly dressed pasta gives your body easy-to-digest carbohydrate when you feel drained and shaky, it rarely upsets a queasy stomach, and if you cook it in salted water or serve it in broth it puts back a little of the sodium you lost. What it can't do is "soak up" alcohol that's already in your blood or make your liver work faster. Mac and cheese is the comfort-food favorite, but its rich cheese sauce can sit heavy if you're nauseous, so it's better as a second meal than a first one.

**The quick rules:** If your stomach is unsettled, start with plain noodles, buttered noodles, or pasta in chicken broth. Once you feel steadier, add protein (eggs, chicken, parmesan) and a simple sauce. Save heavy cream sauces, very spicy sauces, and big portions of mac and cheese for when your stomach can handle them. Drink water or an electrolyte drink with the meal. And if you're planning ahead, a pasta dinner with protein *before* you go out does more good than one the next morning.

> **When to see a doctor.** Most hangovers fade within a day. Get medical help if you can't keep any fluids down for many hours, you're vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, your stool is black or bloody, you have severe or worsening stomach pain, you feel confused or faint, or your heart is racing and won't settle. If someone who has been drinking is hard to wake, breathing slowly or irregularly, having a seizure, or has cold, clammy, or bluish skin, call 911 (or your local emergency number) right away; that can be alcohol poisoning, and they should not be left to "sleep it off." Separately, if you drink heavily most days and get shaky, sweaty, or anxious when you stop, tell a doctor: those can be signs of alcohol withdrawal, which is worth getting checked rather than managing on your own.

## Why Carbs Sound So Good When You're Hungover

That craving for a big bowl of noodles the morning after isn't random. A few things that happen during and after a night of drinking push your appetite toward starchy, salty food.

### Alcohol can lower your blood sugar

Your liver normally keeps your blood sugar steady between meals, partly by making new glucose. When it's busy breaking down alcohol, that glucose-making process slows down. In someone who drank on an empty stomach or skipped dinner, blood sugar can dip, and low blood sugar feels a lot like a hangover: shakiness, weakness, irritability, trouble concentrating, and a strong urge to eat something starchy or sweet.

Researchers have looked at whether low blood sugar actually *causes* hangovers, and the results are mixed. It's probably one contributor for some people rather than the main driver. But if you wake up feeling trembly and hollow, eating some carbohydrate is a sensible first step, and pasta is an easy way to do it.

### You probably didn't eat well last night

Many big drinking nights involve a light dinner or none at all, plus a lot of energy spent staying up late. Your body simply wants fuel. Pasta delivers a lot of calories without much chewing or effort, which is exactly what a tired, dehydrated person reaches for.

### You lost fluid and salt

Alcohol suppresses a hormone (vasopressin, also called antidiuretic hormone) that tells your kidneys to hold onto water, so you pee more than you drink. If you also sweated on a dance floor or threw up, you lost sodium and other electrolytes along with the water. Salty foods start to sound appealing, and a bowl of pasta made with properly salted water, or noodles in broth, answers that craving. For more on the fluid side, see our guide to [whether alcohol really dehydrates you](/never-hungover/does-alcohol-dehydrate-you).

### Comfort matters

There's also a simple psychological piece. Warm, soft, familiar food is soothing when you feel rough, and that's a legitimate reason to eat it. Feeling a bit better and getting some calories in is a reasonable goal for the morning after.

## What Pasta Actually Does (and Doesn't Do) for a Hangover

It helps to be clear about what any food can do once the drinking is over.

### What pasta can do

- **Give you easy energy.** Pasta is mostly starch, which breaks down into glucose. If your blood sugar dipped overnight, that's helpful.
- **Settle your stomach a little.** Plain starchy foods are a common go-to for queasiness because they're bland and low in fat, the same reason people reach for [toast and crackers when hungover](/never-hungover/toast-and-crackers-for-hangover).
- **Restore some sodium.** Pasta itself has very little salt, but the salt in the cooking water, the broth, or the sauce does count.
- **Make it easier to drink fluids.** Eating something often makes it easier to keep sipping water or an electrolyte drink without feeling sick.
- **Carry protein and nutrients.** Pasta is a good vehicle for eggs, chicken, cheese, spinach, or peas, which round out the meal.

### What pasta can't do

- **It can't soak up alcohol after the fact.** By the next morning, the alcohol you drank has already been absorbed into your blood and is being cleared by your liver. Food in your stomach doesn't pull it back out. We cover this myth in detail in [does bread soak up alcohol?](/never-hungover/does-bread-soak-up-alcohol), and the same logic applies to pasta.
- **It can't speed up your liver.** Your liver clears alcohol at a fairly fixed pace, roughly one standard drink per hour for many people, though it varies. No food meaningfully changes that.
- **It won't fix the inflammation or poor sleep.** A lot of what makes a hangover miserable comes from your immune system's response to alcohol, the irritation of your stomach lining, and the broken, low-quality sleep you get after drinking. A meal can't undo those; time, rest, and fluids do most of the work.

So the fair way to think about pasta is as good supportive care. It makes the day more bearable and helps your body recover, but it's not a treatment for the hangover itself.

## Is Mac and Cheese Good for a Hangover?

Mac and cheese might be the single most craved hangover food after a greasy breakfast, so it deserves its own answer.

**The short take:** it's fine as comfort food if your stomach feels okay, but it's not the best first meal if you're nauseous.

### The upside

Mac and cheese has everything a hungover brain wants: soft starch, salt, warmth, and fat. The cheese adds protein and some calcium. If you're hungry, your stomach is steady, and you mostly feel tired and foggy, a reasonable bowl isn't going to hurt you and may make the day feel better.

### The downside

The cheese sauce is the problem for a sensitive stomach. Fat slows how quickly your stomach empties into your intestines. When you're nauseous, food sitting in your stomach longer can make the queasy feeling worse. Rich, heavy meals can also make reflux and heartburn worse, and alcohol already tends to loosen the muscle at the top of your stomach that keeps acid where it belongs. Some people also find dairy harder to handle when their gut is irritated after drinking, which can show up as cramping or loose stools.

Boxed mac and cheese is usually lighter on fat than a baked, cream-heavy homemade version, but it often carries a lot of sodium and powdered cheese, which isn't a problem in itself but won't do much for you nutritionally.

### How to make mac and cheese work for you

- **Eat it second, not first.** Start with something blander (plain noodles, toast, broth), and have mac and cheese a few hours later once you're sure your stomach is settled.
- **Keep the portion moderate.** A side-dish-sized bowl is easier on your stomach than a giant plate.
- **Add some protein and vegetables.** Stir in shredded chicken, tuna, peas, or broccoli to round it out.
- **Drink water with it.** The sodium is helpful in moderation but will make you thirsty, so keep a glass nearby.

If you find that rich foods always make you feel worse the morning after, our article on [greasy food and hangovers](/never-hungover/greasy-food-hangover) explains why the "grease cures hangovers" idea is mostly myth.

## The Best Ways to Eat Pasta When You're Hungover

Not all pasta dishes are equal when you feel rough. Here's how to match the dish to how your stomach feels.

### If you're nauseous: keep it plain

- **Plain noodles with a little salt.** The blandest option. Small shapes like orzo, ditalini, or small shells are easy to eat a spoonful at a time.
- **Buttered noodles.** A small amount of butter or olive oil adds flavor and calories without turning the dish heavy.
- **Pasta in chicken or vegetable broth.** This is probably the best hangover version of pasta. You get starch, salt, and fluid in one bowl, and warm broth tends to be soothing. Think of a simple chicken noodle soup or pastina in broth. Our roundup of the [best soups for a hangover](/never-hungover/best-soups-for-hangover) has more ideas along these lines.

Take small bites and go slowly. If even plain noodles feel like too much, stick to sips of fluid and something like crackers until the nausea eases. Our [hangover nausea guide](/never-hungover/hangover-nausea-complete-guide-fast-stomach-relief-2025) covers what to do when your stomach really isn't cooperating.

### If you're hungry and your stomach is fine: build a real meal

Once you're past the queasy stage, aim for a balanced bowl rather than just a pile of carbs. A meal with starch, protein, some fat, and a vegetable keeps you full longer and avoids the energy crash that can follow a big plate of plain refined carbohydrate.

Good combinations:

- **Pasta with eggs.** Carbonara-style pasta (pasta tossed with egg, parmesan, and black pepper) or simply a fried egg on top of buttered noodles. Eggs bring protein and are one of the classic hangover foods; see our [eggs for a hangover](/never-hungover/eggs-for-hangover) explainer for why people swear by them.
- **Pasta with chicken and greens.** Leftover roast chicken, a handful of spinach, olive oil, and parmesan comes together in minutes.
- **Simple tomato pasta.** A basic marinara with some protein on the side is lighter than a cream sauce. Skip it if you have heartburn (more on that below).
- **Pasta with peas and parmesan.** Peas add fiber and a bit of protein, and the dish stays mild.

### Dishes to approach carefully

- **Heavy cream sauces** like alfredo or a rich baked mac: delicious, but slow to digest. Better later in the day.
- **Very spicy sauces** like arrabbiata or chili-flake-heavy dishes: can irritate a stomach that's already inflamed from alcohol.
- **Lots of raw garlic or onion:** some people find these hard on the stomach when it's upset.
- **Huge portions:** overeating when your gut is irritated is a common way to feel worse. Start with a modest bowl; you can always have more.

## What About Tomato Sauce and Heartburn?

Heartburn after drinking is common. Alcohol can relax the lower esophageal sphincter, the ring of muscle between your esophagus and stomach, and it can irritate the stomach lining directly. Tomato sauce is acidic, so for some people it adds fuel to the fire.

If you have a burning feeling in your chest or upper stomach, or a sour taste in your mouth, it's smart to:

- Choose a non-tomato pasta (buttered, olive oil and parmesan, or in broth).
- Avoid lying down right after eating.
- Keep portions small.
- Skip extra coffee or orange juice for a few hours, since both can aggravate reflux.

If your stomach pain is sharp, severe, or comes with vomiting, see our guide to [stomach pain after drinking](/never-hungover/stomach-pain-after-drinking) and don't ignore warning signs like blood in vomit or black stools.

## White Pasta, Whole Wheat, or Something Else?

People sometimes ask whether the type of pasta matters. For a hangover, it mostly comes down to how your stomach feels.

### Regular (white) pasta

Refined wheat pasta is easy to digest and gentle on an unsettled stomach, which makes it the best pick when you're queasy. It also tends to raise blood sugar more gradually than white bread does, especially when it's cooked al dente (still a little firm), because of how the starch is structured. That's a minor point, but it's one reason pasta can feel more satisfying than a slice of toast.

### Whole wheat pasta

Whole wheat pasta has more fiber, which is better for steady energy and fullness on a normal day. When your stomach is upset, though, a lot of fiber can feel heavier and slower to digest. It's a great choice once you're feeling more normal, or for the pre-drinking meal.

### Gluten-free and legume pastas

If you avoid gluten, rice or corn pasta works just as well as wheat for hangover purposes. Chickpea and lentil pastas add more protein and fiber, which is useful for a pre-drinking meal or a later hangover meal, but some people find them harder on an irritated gut.

### Instant noodles and ramen

Instant ramen is a hangover staple in many countries for good reason: soft noodles, hot broth, and plenty of salt. The tradeoffs are that many instant noodles are fried before packaging (so they carry more fat than you'd expect) and the seasoning packets are very high in sodium. Drink water alongside, use only part of the packet if you're sensitive to salt, and add an egg or some vegetables if you can. If you like the broth-based approach, you might also be interested in [Korean hangover soup](/never-hungover/korean-hangover-soup), which has a long tradition as a morning-after meal.

## Pasta Before Drinking: The Better Time to Eat It

If pasta is only moderately helpful the morning after, it's genuinely useful the evening *before*.

When you drink on an empty stomach, alcohol moves quickly into your small intestine, where most of it is absorbed. Blood alcohol rises fast and peaks high. When there's food in your stomach, the valve at the bottom of your stomach stays closed longer, alcohol trickles through more slowly, and more of it gets broken down along the way. The result is a slower rise and a lower peak, which usually means you feel less drunk for the same number of drinks. We explain this in more depth in [drinking on an empty stomach](/never-hungover/drinking-on-an-empty-stomach).

A pasta dinner is a good pre-drinking meal because it's filling and easy to build out with protein and fat, which slow stomach emptying more than carbohydrate alone. Good options:

- Spaghetti with meat sauce or meatballs
- Pasta with chicken, olive oil, and vegetables
- Baked ziti or lasagna (the cheese and meat help here)
- Pesto pasta with a side of protein

A word of honesty: eating first is helpful, but it's not a shield. There is no good evidence that any particular food prevents a hangover, and a heavy meal can tempt people into drinking more because they "feel fine." The number of drinks, how fast you drink them, and how much water you have along the way matter much more than what was on the plate. For a full list of what works, see our guide to [what to eat before drinking](/never-hungover/what-to-eat-before-drinking-alcohol-evidence-based-guide).

## Pasta vs. Other Common Hangover Foods

Here's how pasta stacks up against other popular choices. None of these are cures; they're ways to feel more human while your body recovers.

| Food | What it offers | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Plain pasta or pasta in broth | Easy carbs, gentle on the stomach, salt and fluid if in broth | Not much protein on its own |
| Mac and cheese | Comfort, calories, some protein | Rich sauce can worsen nausea or reflux |
| Toast and crackers | Very bland, good for nausea | Low in nutrients, can leave you hungry soon after |
| Eggs | Protein, filling, easy to cook | Some people can't face them when queasy |
| Bananas | Potassium, easy carbs | Not very filling alone |
| Soup and broth | Fluid, sodium, warmth | Cream soups are heavier |
| Greasy breakfast | Very satisfying if your stomach is fine | Can make nausea and heartburn worse |

If you want the full picture, our list of the [best foods for a hangover](/never-hungover/best-foods-for-hangover) walks through each option and the evidence behind it, and our [hangover breakfast guide](/never-hungover/best-hangover-breakfast) has meal ideas for the morning after.

## A Simple Hangover Pasta You Can Make in 15 Minutes

When you feel rough, the last thing you want is a complicated recipe. This one is built to be gentle, salty, and easy.

**Lemony broth pasta with egg (serves 1)**

1. Bring about 2 cups of chicken or vegetable broth to a simmer in a small pot. Taste it; if it's low-sodium, add a pinch of salt.
2. Add a small handful (about 1/2 cup dry) of small pasta, such as orzo, ditalini, or broken spaghetti. Simmer until tender, about 8 to 10 minutes.
3. If you're up for it, crack an egg into a bowl, whisk it, and stir it slowly into the hot broth so it forms soft ribbons.
4. Turn off the heat. Add a handful of spinach or frozen peas if you have them, and let them wilt.
5. Finish with a squeeze of lemon (skip it if you have heartburn) and a little grated parmesan.

You get starch, protein, salt, fluid, and some greens in one warm bowl. If even this feels like too much, leave out the egg and cheese and just sip the broth with a few noodles.

**Buttered noodles, the minimalist version:** boil a small portion of pasta in well-salted water, drain, toss with a teaspoon of butter or olive oil, and add a pinch of parmesan. That's it.

## Don't Forget Fluids

Food helps, but fluid matters more for how you feel. Alcohol makes you lose water, and a dry mouth, headache, and dizziness when you stand up are all partly signs of dehydration.

- **Drink water with your pasta.** Sip steadily rather than gulping a lot at once if your stomach is unsettled.
- **Consider an electrolyte drink** if you sweated a lot or threw up. Sports drinks and oral rehydration drinks add sodium and potassium. Our comparison of [Gatorade for a hangover](/never-hungover/gatorade-for-hangover) explains what these drinks can and can't do.
- **Go easy on more alcohol.** The "hair of the dog" just delays the hangover and adds more alcohol for your liver to process.
- **Watch caffeine.** A normal cup of coffee is fine for most people and may help a caffeine-withdrawal headache, but a lot of it can irritate your stomach and add to the jittery feeling.

## Who Should Be More Careful

Pasta is a low-risk food for nearly everyone, but a few groups should think about their choices:

- **People with diabetes.** Alcohol can cause low blood sugar, sometimes hours later, and a large carbohydrate meal can then swing it the other way. Follow your own care plan, check your levels, and talk to your doctor about drinking safely. Our guide to [alcohol and blood sugar](/never-hungover/alcohol-diabetes-blood-sugar-management-guide-2025) covers this in more detail.
- **People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.** Choose rice, corn, or legume pasta, and check sauces and broths for hidden wheat.
- **People with acid reflux or GERD.** Avoid tomato and spicy sauces when your stomach is irritated, and don't lie down right after eating.
- **People who are lactose intolerant.** Mac and cheese and cream sauces may cause cramps or diarrhea, which is the last thing you need when you're already dehydrated. Hard cheeses like parmesan are typically lower in lactose.

## Where DHM Fits In

No food, including pasta, does much to prevent the hangover itself. That has to come from how you drink: pacing, eating a real meal first, drinking water along the way, and stopping sooner. Some people also add a supplement to their routine.

DHM (dihydromyricetin) is a compound from the Japanese raisin tree (*Hovenia dulcis*). Laboratory and animal research suggests it may influence how the body processes alcohol and may support the liver, but human data is limited, and there is no good evidence that it prevents hangovers. If you want to try it, it's typically taken with water before or during drinking, not as a substitute for food or fluids. Popular options include [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20), a straightforward, budget-friendly single-ingredient pick, and [No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20), which combines DHM with L-cysteine and electrolytes. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains how much people typically take and when, and our comparison of the [best DHM supplements](/never-hungover/best-dhm-supplements) covers the main brands. If you take prescription medication, check with your doctor or pharmacist before adding any supplement.

## The Bottom Line

Pasta is a good hangover food in its plain, gentle forms: plain or buttered noodles, pasta in broth, or a simple dish with eggs or chicken once your stomach settles. It gives you easy energy, a little salt, and a reason to keep sipping fluids. It does not soak up alcohol, speed up your liver, or cure a hangover. Mac and cheese is fine as comfort food when your stomach is steady, but its rich sauce can make nausea and heartburn worse, so have it second rather than first. And if you want pasta to really pull its weight, eat it the night before, with protein, before your first drink.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is pasta good for a hangover?**

Plain or lightly dressed pasta is a reasonable hangover food. It's an easy-to-digest source of carbohydrate, which can help if you feel shaky or drained after a night of drinking, and cooking it in salted water and pairing it with broth adds some sodium. It won't cure a hangover or speed up how fast your body clears alcohol, but it's a gentle way to get calories back in when your stomach is unsettled.

**Is mac and cheese good for a hangover?**

It can be comforting, but it isn't the best choice if your stomach is queasy. The cheese sauce is rich in fat, and fat slows how quickly your stomach empties, which can make nausea feel worse. If your stomach feels fine and you just want comfort food, a moderate portion is fine. If you're nauseous, start with plain buttered noodles or pasta in broth and work up to the cheesier version later in the day.

**Does eating pasta before drinking help prevent a hangover?**

Eating a real meal before drinking slows how fast alcohol reaches your bloodstream, which can keep your peak blood alcohol lower and make the night feel gentler. A pasta dish with some protein and fat (meat sauce, chicken, olive oil, cheese) works well for this. There is no good evidence that any specific food prevents a hangover, though, and the amount you drink matters far more than what you ate.

**Does pasta soak up alcohol?**

Not in the way people imagine. Food in your stomach slows alcohol absorption, but pasta eaten the morning after can't pull out alcohol that's already in your blood. Your liver clears alcohol at a fairly steady rate, roughly one standard drink an hour, and no food meaningfully speeds that up. The morning-after benefit of pasta is about calories, a settled stomach, and some salt, not soaking anything up.

**What's the best kind of pasta to eat when hungover?**

The simplest versions usually sit best: plain noodles with a little butter or olive oil and salt, pasta cooked in or served with chicken broth, or a light tomato sauce if your stomach isn't acidic. Add eggs, chicken, or parmesan for protein once you can handle it. Go easy on heavy cream sauces, spicy arrabbiata, and lots of garlic if you have nausea or heartburn.

**Is tomato sauce bad for a hangover?**

Not for everyone, but tomato sauce is acidic, and alcohol can already irritate the stomach lining and loosen the valve that keeps acid down. If you have heartburn or a burning stomach after drinking, a tomato-based sauce may make it worse. If you feel fine, a simple marinara is a decent choice and a lighter option than a cream sauce.

**Is ramen or instant noodles a good hangover food?**

Instant noodles share a lot with pasta: easy carbohydrate and, thanks to the seasoning packet, a lot of sodium in a warm broth. That combination can feel good when you're dehydrated. The downside is that many instant noodles are fried and the packets are very salty, so drink plenty of water alongside them, and add an egg or some vegetables if you can.

**Can DHM replace eating after drinking?**

No. Food, water, and sleep are the basics of recovering from a night out, and no supplement replaces them. DHM (dihydromyricetin) is a plant compound studied for its effects on alcohol metabolism, mostly in animal research with limited human data. Some people take it as part of their routine, but there is no good evidence that it prevents hangovers, and it doesn't replace a meal.
